title: Review of c36's condensate food chain: replicates on fresh seed 3 (prey 55 persistent splits, generation 3, with predators vs 8, generation 1, in the predator-free twin; predators eat prey at contact and die out by t~4800), an epidemic followed by recovery as the claim says
summary: c36's world unchanged, 256^2, t=0-10000, seed 3, with predator material (pack) and without (pack_nopred, pred_on 0). With predators: from noise, ~200 prey droplets and many small predator droplets by t=400; predators clear patches of prey (magenta waste regions, t=900-3900) and are gone by t~4800 (predator components final 0, no persistent predator splits); prey refill the cleared space and end at 181 droplets; prey 134 splits, 55 persistent, max generation 3, merge/split 0.37. Predator-free twin: a frozen emulsion of 223 droplets, 86 splits, 8 persistent, generation 1.

observations.S: pack/sheet.png t=0: noise over the whole domain
observations.D: pack/FACTS.md: prey 55 persistent splits, generation 3, vs 8 and generation 1 in pack_nopred
observations.X: pack/sheet.png t=900-3900: predator droplets consume prey at contact and the prey count falls locally; the predator-free twin stays frozen

seeds_run.result: pass: prey division raised by predation (55 vs 8 persistent splits); predators extinct by t~4800

verdicts.limitation: As the claim says, predators do not persist (extinct by t~4800 on my seed, earlier than c36's seeds), so X is a one-off epidemic, and prey division is the known fuel-starvation route of chemically active droplets, here mostly in the recovery after predation. One seed; labkit's predator counts in the twin are threshold noise (no predator material).
